## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Piṅgiyamāṇavapucchā* ("The Questions of the Student Piṅgiya") is a discourse in the *Pārāyanavagga* of the *Suttanipāta* (Snp 5.17, verses 1120–1123, PTS Snp 217) [Norman 1997-2001; Hazra 1994; SuttaCentral]. Composed in the Triṣṭubh metre, the text depicts the student Piṅgiya, who is troubled by the deterioration of his aging body, asking the Buddha how to transcend birth and decay [Norman 1997-2001; SuttaCentral]. In response, the Buddha explains that one overcomes birth and decay by abandoning the physical body and desire, cultivating the intention of not coming into renewed existence [Hazra 1994].
